extracted.intended_audience: British legislators and literate public concerned with the French Revolution and constitutional design
extracted.subtask_description: A political-philosophical critique of the French revolutionary constitution that articulates principles and warnings for constructing durable republican and executive institutions. Focuses on representation, classes, money/paper currency, provincial attachments, and the balance of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of citizens into appropriate classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispose their citizens into such classes, and to place them in such situations in the state, as their peculiar habits might qualify them to fill, and to allot to them such appropriated privileges as might secure to them what their specific occasions required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislators of antiquity studied 'human nature' and classed citizens by birth, education, profession, residence and property to create stability and to furnish each description with force to protect it in conflicts of interest. Proper classification is described as 'good in all forms of government' and 'a strong barrier against the excesses of despotism.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confound all citizens into a homogeneous mass
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attempting to confound all sorts of citizens... into one homogeneous mass; do not reduce men to loose counters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay warns that metaphysical or egalitarian schemes that abolish distinctions produce 'a number of incoherent republics' and destroy the practical bonds and roles that allow a commonwealth to function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation must serve the whole under a standing fundamental government
rubrics_metrics.description: Each deputy to the Assembly would be the representative of France, and of all its descriptions... This standing, unalterable, fundamental government would make... that territory truly and properly a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should originate in and point to an enduring central government (a 'government of reference') rather than making the elective assembly the sole sovereign; otherwise the parts cannot cohere into a durable whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct accountability of representatives to the people
rubrics_metrics.description: The member who goes to the National Assembly is not chosen by the people, nor accountable to them... In your elections responsibility cannot exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple intermediary elections (three elections, two sets of magistracy) sever the connection between constituent and representative, preventing voters from knowing fitness or holding representatives to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections must permit voters to know candidate fitness and retain leverage over them
rubrics_metrics.description: To answer its real purposes, you must first possess the means of knowing the fitness of your man; and then you must retain some hold upon him by personal obligation or dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An election's purpose is defeated if primary electors cannot judge candidates' qualities or cannot exert authoritative instruction; electoral design should enable assessment and obligate representatives to constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid circuitous gradations of election that eliminate personal choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all the powers unfit to be delegated... that most peculiarly unfit is what relates to a personal choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a personal choice is repeatedly delegated across intermediary bodies, it becomes impossible to attribute responsibility or to effect corrective accountability; circuitous election chains produce confusion and false appearance of election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disqualify representatives so soon after service that expertise is lost
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man who has served in an Assembly is ineligible for two years after... Just as these magistrates begin to learn their trade, like chimney-sweepers, they are disqualified for exercising it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibiting immediate re-election wastes acquired experience and produces superficial, interrupted, and broken governance; terms and ineligibilities should preserve continuity and competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an intermediate senate or council to provide steadiness
rubrics_metrics.description: They have forgot to constitute a senate, or something of that nature and character... It holds a sort of middle place between the supreme power exercised by the people... and the mere executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A republican government generally requires a body that gives 'bias and steadiness', provides a point of connection for foreign states, and preserves consistency in proceedings; omission is a 'sovereign incapacity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive must possess deliberative discretion and means of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive magistracy... ought to be environed with dignity, authority, and consideration, and it ought to lead to glory. The office of execution is an office of exertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executives need real powers and incentives to perform duties faithfully; an executive without discretion or means to reward service will preside over perfunctory or fearful compliance rather than zealous administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: The sovereign/executive should be the fountain of justice and honor
rubrics_metrics.description: The king of France is not the fountain of justice... He is not even the public prosecutor... He is no more the fountain of honor than he is the fountain of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stripping the executive of judicial nomination, pardon, suspension, and honorific powers degrades the office, prevents it from naturally attracting loyal and capable subordinates, and leaves only odious coercive functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making the executive a mere instrument for enforcement without reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who serve the king can be actuated by no natural motive but fear,—by a fear of everything except their master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without permanent offices, grants, titles, or pensions under the executive, those who execute orders act from fear; law cannot easily enforce zeal or faithful devotion when natural motives (rewards, honor) are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on confiscation and forced paper currency as durable state cement
rubrics_metrics.description: The confiscation, with the compulsory paper currency annexed to it... may for some time compose some sort of cement, but... if... insufficient to support the paper coinage... it will add infinitely to the dissociation, distraction, and confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation plus forced paper money can temporarily bind disparate republics but risks destroying coherence and producing instability if the currency or its backing fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware concentration of monetary power in managers (oligarchy risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper circulation... must put the whole of what power, authority, and influence is left... into the hands of the managers and conductors of this circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state that substitutes paper currency without real backing hands enormous influence to financiers and directors, creating an oligarchic class that can dominate politics and land through monetary operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid founding a commonwealth on speculation and gaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Your legislators, in everything new, are the very first who have founded a commonwealth upon gaming... to make speculation as extensive as life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the state's life is tied to speculation (assignats, lotteries, funds) industry, economy, thrift, and accumulation are undermined: people cannot plan or save if value is unstable, leading to social decay and exploitation by the few who 'understand the game.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve provincial, historic, and local attachments over geometric divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: No man ever was attached by a sense of pride, partiality, or real affection, to a description of square measurement... We begin our public affections in our families. We pass on to our neighborhoods, and our habitual provincial connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitrary 'geometrical' divisions (squares, numbered districts) cannot replace the organic bonds of neighborhood and province that teach civic attachment and scale up to love of the whole nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-centralization of power in the capital (Paris)
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of the city of Paris is evidently one great spring of all their politics... It is through the power of Paris, now become the centre and focus of jobbing, that the leaders of this faction direct, or rather command, the whole legislative and the whole executive government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compact, concentrated capital that dominates legislative and executive life can hold subordinate regions weak and disunited, preventing confederation or effective resistance and producing long-term instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully consider the composition and powers of the judicature
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the new Constitution, the higher parts of judicature, in either of its lines, are not in the king. The judges... are of his nomination. He neither proposes the candidates nor has a negative on the choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay criticizes arrangements that remove judicial origination and control from a coordinating authority; the design of judicial appointment and the relation to the executive and sovereign affect dignity, responsibility, and administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against making representatives ephemeral and only election-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: As, in the end, all the members of this elective Constitution are equally fugitive, and exist only for the election, they may be no longer the same persons who had chosen him, to whom he is to be responsible when he solicits for a renewal of his trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If members are transient and oriented solely to periodic election, they cannot be held meaningfully responsible and lose continuity; institutional design should create lasting obligations and connections between electors and representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class distinctions serve as indirect restraints preventing despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: Every such classification, if properly ordered, is good in all forms of government, and composes a strong barrier against the excesses of despotism, as well as it is the necessary means of giving effect and permanence to a republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly ordered social distinctions and intermediate bodies provide indirect checks on power; their removal eliminates the mitigations of despotism and endangers future arbitrary rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid levelling and crushing traditional orders and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: They have levelled and crushed together all the orders which they found... They reduce men to loose counters, merely for the sake of simple telling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radical abolition of historical mediating institutions (ecclesiastical, provincial, corporate) removes the social scaffolding that cultivates civic habits and practical cooperation, risking incoherence and weakness in the state.
